findings.title: Backup code login bypasses password check
findings.body: The password check is guarded by `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`, so when a backupCode is supplied with no totpCode the password is verified. But a request with `totpCode` set (any value) skips the password check entirely, and the same applies to the new backup-code branch. An attacker who submits email + a valid backup code and a dummy totpCode would skip the password. Even without a dummy totpCode, the check must be restructured so password is always required for CAL users; with this change a backup code is only effective as a second factor if the first factor is enforced independently of totpCode.

findings.title: Backup code comparison and handling are fragile (null codes, non-string input)
findings.body: Used codes are set to null in the array and re-saved. `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` is a plain non-constant-time comparison, fine in practice, but the lookup is not atomic: two concurrent logins with the same code can both read the array before either writes back, so a single-use code can be reused (read-modify-write race). There is also no per-attempt rate limit specific to backup codes beyond the generic limiter.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode type can crash the endpoint
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called on user-controlled JSON; if backupCode is a non-string truthy value (number, object) this throws a TypeError and returns a 500 rather than a 400. Also JSON.parse of the decrypted codes isn't guarded. Validate that backupCode is a string first.

findings.title: Throwing errors in API handler instead of returning a response
findings.body: Missing encryption key in the backup-code branch does `throw new Error(...)`, producing an unhandled 500 with no JSON body, while the modal expects `body.error` from `response.json()`. This can cause a JSON parse failure in the client; the setup endpoint returns a proper 500 JSON for the same condition.

findings.title: Backup codes overwritten on each setup call and returned before 2FA confirmed
findings.body: Backup codes are generated and persisted at setup time, before the user has verified the TOTP code, and are regenerated whenever setup is re-run (e.g. cancel and retry). The stored codes are only shown after enable succeeds, and the state is not reset on cancel except password/step; if the user cancels, backupCodes remain in DB with twoFactorEnabled=false. This is mostly harmless but stale codes linger.

findings.title: Modal can be dismissed without ever showing/saving backup codes; state not reset
findings.body: After enable succeeds the step moves to DisplayBackupCodes, but the Dialog's onOpenChange (outside click/Esc) closes the dialog without calling resetState/onEnable. The parent's switch state then isn't updated and the modal re-opens at the backup-codes step with the old codes; also the onEnable callback (which refreshes 2FA status) is only called through the Close button. Additionally the blob URL is never revoked on unmount, and `useState([])` is typed as never[].

findings.title: Component misnamed TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export of BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, duplicating the other component's name and confusing stack traces and devtools.

findings.title: Toggle button defaults to submit and BackupCode `required` interferes with form
findings.body: The 'Lost access' Button has no `type="button"`; depending on Button's default it may submit the form inside the Form. In addition, `required` on the BackupCode field plus switching modes with `resetForm` leaves the hidden TwoFactor input registered with no value, and `required` was newly added to PasswordField even when the user is passwordless-protected.

findings.title: No tests for backup code login or disable flows
findings.body: The core new behavior (logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement, disabling with a backup code, invalid code errors) has no test coverage; the PR only adds download/copy/close checks and leaves a TODO. The PR checklist admits no tests were added.
